newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat emergence nears 100 percent.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat emergence nears 100 percent.

text.p: Texas' wheat crop approached 100 percent emergence during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
Cloudy, damp conditions covered most of northern Texas and the Plains areas, while dry, windy conditions dominated most of central and southern Texas.
Irrigation of small grains fields in the High Plains remained active while dryland fields were in need of moisture.
Cotton harvest was slightly ahead of average, although many producers in north central Texas were still waiting for a freeze before harvesting.
Wheat emerged 99 percent vs 94 week ago, 75 year ago, 78 on a five-year average.
Wheat rated 74 percent of normal, vs 69 w/a, 55 y/a.
Sorghum harvested 94 percent vs 89 w/a, 97 y/a, 95 avg.
Cotton bolls opening 99 percent vs 97 w/a, 96 y/a, 96 avg.
Cotton harvested 60 percent vs 47 w/a, 58 y/a, 59 avg.
Cotton rated 68 percent good/excellent vs 65 w/a, 60 y/a.
Pasture and range condition was rated 36 percent good to excellent, versus 34 percent at that level last week.
